result.title: When AI Agents Should Repair, Replan, or Abandon: A Threshold Theory of Plan Commitment
result.summary: AI agents often discover mid-execution that their plan is broken, for example when an action fails or a tool is withdrawn. Deployed systems use conventions such as retry loops or "always replan," and a recent benchmark finds no fixed strategy dominates. This paper derives the optimal policy. In the model, a disruption destroys the causal support of part of a plan; repair is a partial reset that preserves the plan's structure, replanning is a full reset, and changing a plan is costly because others have conditioned on it. The optimal policy is a threshold in effective disruption depth: repair shallow damage, replan after deep damage, and abandon the goal when even a fresh plan is not worth its cost. Depth depends on plan structure. In expectation, a single broken action forces 1+R(G)/n actions to be revalidated, where R(G) counts the pairs of actions joined by a dependency path; to first order, a fully serial plan switches to replanning at raw damage about w times smaller than a plan of w parallel chains. A closed-form stability-price threshold determines when a worse repaired plan should be kept over a better fresh one. As language-model planners push replanning costs toward zero, the stability price becomes the only force sustaining plan commitment. Under repeated disruptions, revision frictions make commitment hysteresis optimal: the agent keeps executing a plan it would never choose fresh, and each repair adds patch debt until the debt outweighs repair's cost advantage and the agent rebuilds. A value-of-diagnosis result states when measuring damage is worth its compute and shows that "always replan" is optimal when damage is predictably deep and replanning is the better fallback. A separately implemented numerical checker tests each proposition (zero violations; 1.6 million static-model evaluations), and the model's regime map reproduces that benchmark's regime flips qualitatively.

AI.brief_summary: 该文从理论上推导智能体计划受损后的最优应对策略：以「有效损伤深度」为阈值，浅损伤局部修复、深损伤完全重规划、若新计划不值其成本则放弃目标；并给出稳定性价格阈值、反复损伤下的承诺滞后（patch debt）、以及「诊断价值」何时值得花算力测量损伤的结论，配合数值检查器验证各命题。
AI.relevance_reason: 修复（保留结构的部分重置）与重规划（全量重置）的区分、以及诊断信息价值的阈值判断，可能为 LVR 中「何时刷新/重建 latent 推理状态、何时继续获取视觉证据、何时停止」的 THINK/LOOK/STOP 成本权衡提供形式化参照，但其成本模型基于计划依赖结构，能否迁移到多模态推理需核查。
